subject: NavSpark - request to combine startup subsidy with committed discount
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex@navspark.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: combine startup subsidy with committed discount and billing linkage

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team and I are excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. Quick ask as we move toward a pilot: our accelerator provides a $20k sandbox subsidy that we'd like to apply against onboarding costs if we convert to Dedicated within 120 days.

Two specific questions:
1) Can Redwood apply our accelerator subsidy as an account credit that can be used toward a Dedicated commitment (we'd like it to offset first-month committed fees)?
2) Are there any tax / invoicing requirements on your side for the subsidy (we need a line-item for our sponsor's accounting)?

We're also evaluating a short-term committed discount if we move to Dedicated (looking for ~15% for six months) to make the math work for our board. Is there a standard playbook or an exception path for combining marketing/accelerator subsidies + a conversion discount?

I've attached a one-page summary of the accelerator subsidy. Happy to hop on a call today or tomorrow — what works for you?

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Platform, NavSpark
Alex.Kim@navspark.com
Attachment: NAV_invoice_summary.pdf (1 page, PDF)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex@navspark.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: combine startup subsidy with committed discount and billing linkage

Hi Alex — great to hear and congrats on the accelerator win. Short answers up front: yes, we can often apply accelerator subsidies as an account credit; and yes, we will provide an invoice/addendum that meets sponsor accounting needs.

I'd like to confirm a few guardrails before I send a proposed term sheet:
- Subsidy amount to be applied as a one-time account credit (please confirm $20,000)
- Credit validity window (we typically set 90–180 days). Do you need 120 days?
- Committed discount for Dedicated: we'll route for a temporary conversion discount; need approval from pricing ops for 15% x 6 months.

I've looped in Marissa (Customer Success) and Ben (Enterprise Sales) to help with the convert-to-dedicated workflow and to coordinate billing/addendum. Can you confirm the sponsor requires the subsidy to be reflected on Redwood's invoice (line item name) or if a signed acknowledgment is sufficient?

If that matches, I'll draft a short addendum and get internal approvals (finance / pricing) — target turnaround 48 hours. Available for a 30-minute call Wednesday 10–11am PT if that works.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Redwood Inference — Developer-first LLM inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: NavSpark - subsidy / committed discount request — need sign-off

Forwarding NavSpark's ask. Key points: 20k accelerator subsidy they'd like routed as an account credit usable against Dedicated onboarding if they convert within ~120 days; they also want a 15% committed discount for 6 months on Dedicated.

Proposed internal guardrails (draft):
1) Apply accelerator subsidy as a one-time account credit applied to first invoice after conversion if conversion occurs within 120 days from credit issue.
2) Credit capped at $20,000; non-transferable and non-refundable.
3) Conversion discount: 15% for 6 months on one Dedicated plan, requires 6-month minimum commit.
4) Finance needs a line-item on our invoice: "Accelerator subsidy credit - NavSpark" for sponsor reconciliation.
5) Offer limited to US-region accounts and subject to final credit/contract addendum.

Marissa — ok operationally for onboarding and customer success?
Ben — ok from a pricing / deal desk perspective?
Irene (Finance) — any tax/invoicing concerns if we put the subsidy as a line-item credit on our invoice? Also flag any revenue recognition issues if we apply the credit against committed revenue.

I've attached a draft term sheet (proposed_term_sheet.docx) — very short. If we agree, I'll send to Alex with a DocuSign addendum.

Thanks,
Neha

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 14:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: NavSpark - subsidy / committed discount request — need sign-off

Thanks for laying this out, Neha. I'm okay with the approach with two tweaks:
- Cap the conversion discount exposure by setting a $25k ARR-equivalent floor for the six-month window (keeps economics protected if they convert very small).
- Only allow the subsidy-credit + conversion discount once per account — prevent stacking with other promos.

Irene — can Finance confirm that adding a line-item "Accelerator subsidy credit - NavSpark" will be sufficient for sponsor accounting and that we can apply the credit to the customer's first committed invoice without adverse revrec treatment? If not, we can instead issue a signed acknowledgment + credit memo.

If Finance signs off, I approve routing this as an exception for this deal. Neha — with your go-ahead I'll prepare the addendum for signature (DocuSign).

- Ben
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex@navspark.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: combine startup subsidy with committed discount and billing linkage

Alex — good news. Internal approvals complete. Below is the agreed path and next steps; I've tried to keep it compact so your sponsor has what they need for accounting.

Agreed terms (summary):
- Subsidy: NavSpark's $20,000 accelerator subsidy will be issued as an account credit on Redwood's ledger, titled "Accelerator subsidy credit - NavSpark." The credit will be available for 180 days from issuance; if NavSpark converts to a Dedicated commitment within 120 days of credit issue, the credit will be applied to the first committed invoice.
- Conversion discount: If NavSpark signs a 6-month Dedicated commitment within 120 days, Redwood will apply a 15% discount to the first 6 months of Dedicated service. Discount is limited to one Dedicated plan and will not stack with other promotional discounts. Additionally, the effective ARR exposure will be floored at $25k for discount calculations to protect pricing.
- Documentation: We'll send a one-page addendum for signature (DocuSign) that reflects the credit line-item and conversion discount. Finance confirmed they can include the subsidy as an invoice line item for sponsor reconciliation; they recommended we include sponsor name and reference number on the invoice.
- Next steps: I attached the short addendum and the invoice stub. Please review and (if good) sign the DocuSign link below. Once signed, we'll issue the credit and schedule conversion onboarding if/when you commit.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/sign/verify/EXAMPLE-NavSpark-Addendum
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345-NSK
Drive folder (supporting docs): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bNavSpark-Onboarding

If you'd like to talk through the mechanics, I'm available Thursday 9–10am PT.

Thanks and looking forward,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
